title: Confession and Cipher
premise: Estate lawyer Jude Oyelaran is summoned to probate a will for a man who died three years ago, and the will's existence means someone forged it, or someone faked his death. Twin anonymous letters arrive: one confessing to the old man's murder, the other promising that Jude will 'get their turn' next. As Jude traces the forged will through Lagos's back channels, they realize the killer is someone with access to the original case file, someone who has been watching them for years, and the confession letter was bait. Jude must decide whether to hand their evidence to a corrupt police contact or spring their own trap, and in the final confrontation they learn the killer is the 'dead' man himself, alive and punishing the family who tried to bury him. Jude survives by choosing truth over loyalty, testifying to their own small complicity, and the case closes with justice served outside any courtroom.
about_author: Quentin Okonkwo is a former legal clerk in Lagos who turned to fiction after a decade of watching probate disputes curdle into violence. He writes mysteries about the paperwork of death and the people who hide inside it.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A courier delivers a notarized will for Chief Adebayo Salami, dead three years, and the signature page carries a date after the death certificate. Jude's professional calm cracks into dread as they realize probating it could expose them. Beat: quiet unease sharpening into fear.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Two envelopes arrive the same evening: one confessing to Salami's murder in careful, legalistic prose; the other promising that Jude will 'get their turn.' No return address, no fingerprints. Beat: the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: The Case File
chapters.summary: Jude visits retired inspector Danjuma, who worked the original Salami death, and finds his copy of the file has pages missing, the same pages the letters quote verbatim. Beat: the chilling realization the killer knows the file better than the police did.

chapters.title: Family Portrait
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. At the Salami compound, three heirs perform grief they don't feel: son Tobi, daughter Ronke, second wife Mrs. Salami. Each has an alibi for a death three years old. Beat: surface civility over buried rot.

chapters.title: What Jude Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter in Jude's POV. Years ago, Jude notarized a document they suspected was false for a desperate client and said nothing. The confession letter quotes a phrase from that night, a phrase only one other person could know. Beat: guilt resurfacing.

chapters.title: The Corrupt Friend
chapters.summary: Jude brings the letters to police contact Inspector Eghosa, who offers to bury the case for a fee, revealing the original Salami investigation was closed the same way. Beat: loyalty to an old friend curdling into distrust.

chapters.title: Second Death
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The compound's longtime gardener, who signed as witness on the forged will, is found drowned in a cistern, a ciphered note in his pocket. Beat: the game turns lethal.

chapters.title: Cipher One
chapters.summary: Jude and Danjuma decode the gardener's note: a substitution cipher keyed to the Salami family Bible. It reads: 'He signed because they made him. Ask who they are.' Beat: first real thread of hope.

chapters.title: Ronke's Ledger
chapters.summary: Jude tails Ronke to a marina office and photographs a ledger of payments from the Salami estate to an offshore shell company, monthly, continuing after the death. Beat: the dead man's money is still moving.

chapters.title: Tobi's Debts
chapters.summary: Tobi, drunk and frightened, tells Jude he received a letter too, demanding money or the truth comes out. He assumes Jude is the blackmailer. Beat: paranoia fracturing the family.

chapters.title: The Missing Pages
chapters.summary: Danjuma admits he sold the missing file pages years ago to a private investigator to pay a debt. He doesn't know the buyer's name. Beat: betrayal, and a new lead.

chapters.title: The Investigator
chapters.summary: Jude finds the PI's shuttered office, ransacked before them, and retrieves one discarded scrap: a surveillance photo of Jude themselves, taken years before the letters began. Beat: the watcher has been watching a long time.

chapters.title: Mrs. Salami's Silence
chapters.summary: The second wife, alone, tells Jude her husband was a cruel man and that she prayed for his death, then recants and orders Jude out. Beat: sympathy entangled with suspicion.

chapters.title: Cipher Two
chapters.summary: A second ciphered letter arrives, this one addressed to Tobi, and Jude intercepts it. Decoded, it lists the exact time and method of the gardener's murder, proof the sender was present. Beat: the killer is confessing in installments.

chapters.title: Eghosa's Offer
chapters.summary: Eghosa reveals he knows about Jude's old notarized forgery and offers protection in exchange for Jude handing over all the ciphers, which he would quietly lose. Beat: the price of survival made explicit.

chapters.title: The Shell Company
chapters.summary: Following the ledger money, Jude traces the shell company to a nominee director: a name that matches a junior clerk from the original inquest. Beat: the conspiracy has bureaucratic roots.

chapters.title: The Clerk's Flat
chapters.summary: Jude and Danjuma break into the clerk's flat and find it staged like a shrine to the Salami case: clippings, timelines, photographs, including the missing file pages. The clerk is gone. Beat: obsession made visible.

chapters.title: Ronke's Bargain
chapters.summary: Ronke corners Jude and admits she and her brother paid someone years ago to make their father 'disappear from their lives,' insisting they never asked how. She offers Jude money to stop asking. Beat: loyalty versus truth, priced.

chapters.title: Jude Refuses
chapters.summary: Jude declines the money, and that night their office is searched, files rifled, the forged will stolen. Beat: the cost of integrity arrives immediately.

chapters.title: The Copy
chapters.summary: Jude reveals to Danjuma they kept a photographic copy of the will, hidden with a trusted paralegal. But the paralegal has stopped answering calls. Beat: dread tightening.

chapters.title: The Paralegal
chapters.summary: Jude finds the paralegal unharmed but terrified, paid a visit by a man who quoted Jude's old forgery back to her word for word. She describes his voice: calm, educated, familiar. Beat: the killer is close enough to touch.

chapters.title: Cipher Three
chapters.summary: The third cipher, left in Jude's car, decodes to a confession that contradicts the first letter: different method, different night. One of the confessions is false, and the killer wants Jude to know it. Beat: the ground shifting.

chapters.title: Two Confessions
chapters.summary: Jude and Danjuma compare the letters against the autopsy record and conclude the first confession is a forgery designed to steer them, meaning the second may be real. Beat: method over panic; the trap inverts.

chapters.title: Eghosa's Mistake
chapters.summary: Jude baits Eghosa with a fabricated detail and watches it surface in an anonymous letter within a day: Eghosa is leaking to the killer, or is the killer's instrument. Beat: the last trusted institution falls.

chapters.title: The Inquest Clerk
chapters.summary: The clerk from the shell company is found alive but catatonic in a church, murmuring a name over and over. Danjuma recognizes it: the name of the man whose death certificate Jude has been probating. Beat: the dead man has a name that won't stay buried.

chapters.title: Chief Salami Lives
chapters.summary: Jude confirms it: Salami faked his death three years ago with his children's money and a bought certificate, then began eliminating everyone who helped, one ciphered confession at a time. Beat: the vertigo of the premise fully revealed.

chapters.title: Why Jude
chapters.summary: Danjuma realizes Salami's letters quote Jude's old forgery because Salami's fixer was the client who brought it, the whole chain runs through Jude's one sin. Jude was never random; Jude was always on the list. Beat: guilt and terror fused.

chapters.title: The Children's Choice
chapters.summary: Jude confronts Tobi and Ronke with the truth of their father's survival. Ronke wants to run; Tobi, hollowed out, wants to end it. Beat: the family's loyalty to a monster finally breaking.

chapters.title: Setting the Trap
chapters.summary: Jude drafts a forged letter of their own, using Salami's own cipher, inviting him to retrieve the stolen will copy from the office at a set hour, with Danjuma and a reluctant, honest officer staked out. Beat: the hunted becomes the hunter.

chapters.title: Eghosa's Choice
chapters.summary: Jude gives Eghosa a final chance to come clean; he warns them instead, tipping Salami, and is recorded doing it. Beat: betrayal documented, loyalty finally priced and refused.

chapters.title: The Empty Hour
chapters.summary: The stakeout: Salami doesn't come, but his fixer does, and in the scramble the office catches fire. Jude goes back in for the cipher evidence and nearly dies. Beat: sacrifice and smoke.

chapters.title: What the Fire Left
chapters.summary: Salvaged from the fire: the fixer's briefcase, containing the original faked death certificate and a ledger of everyone paid to stay silent, Jude's own name among them. Beat: evidence and shame in the same hand.

chapters.title: The Confession That Was True
chapters.summary: The fixer, arrested, confirms the second confession was Salami's own: the gardener's drowning, the clerk's breaking, all Salami's hands. Beat: the ciphered confessions finally cohere.

chapters.title: Salami's Summons
chapters.summary: Salami contacts Jude directly, offering the thing Jude most wants: destruction of the record of Jude's old forgery, in exchange for the ledger and silence. Beat: the price of survival offered one last time.

chapters.title: The Meeting
chapters.summary: Jude agrees to meet at the abandoned marina office where the ledger trail began, wearing a wire, knowing Salami will search for one. Beat: controlled terror, the calm before.

chapters.title: Confession and Cipher
chapters.summary: Climax. Salami disarms Jude and delivers his real confession, monologue as verdict, but Jude has hidden the ledger's key page inside the ciphered letter Salami demanded, and the recording is running. Tobi arrives, and Salami falters at his son's face. Beat: truth as weapon.

chapters.title: The Arrest
chapters.summary: The honest officer and Danjuma close in; Salami nearly escapes by boat, but Ronke, arriving unannounced, blocks the dock and lets herself be seen. He surrenders to his children's eyes. Beat: justice without a courtroom's blessing.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Jude testifies, and when asked about the old forgery, confesses to it themselves, surrendering their license and their clean record with the evidence. Beat: the price of survival paid in full, willingly.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: The real will is located and read; the estate dissolves into restitution for the gardener's family and the broken clerk. Tobi and Ronke leave the compound for good. Beat: grief without glamour, order without triumph.

chapters.title: The Last Letter
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A final envelope arrives: Salami, from prison, ciphered, thanking Jude for being the only honest person in the chain. Jude decodes it, reads it twice, and burns it. Beat: quiet, earned closure, invisibility chosen at last.
